page.layout: One printed page of running text, centred in the left half of the scan. Margin notes in the left margin, at the foot of the column: "Aquin." and "1. 2 qu. 96. art. 4." The right edge shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Petrus, Act. 12. 6. Cubavit [illegible, ~9 letters] ἁλύσει[?] δυσί. Nec poteft cuiquam effe dubium, quin possit aliquis ad id officium quod ipsi ex Lege Divina praestandum incumbit, non obstante illa obligatione, denuo se obligare Voto, vel Juramento, vel Promissione. Quemadmodum vovit Jacobus Patri-archa, unicum sibi Deum fore Jehovam, Gen. 28[?]. 21. Et David juravit justa se Dei judicia custoditurum. Psal. 119. 106[?]. Et quotquot fumus Christiani, cum sacro fonte tingeremur, novo nomine baptismali obstrinximus ad fidem in Christum, ad abrenunciandum Satanae, Seculo, Carni; ad observanda Dei mandata: ad quae tamen omnia praestanda nos ante Obligatos fuisse certissimum est.

XI. Conclusio Tertia. Leges Humanae, (sive illicita imperentur, sive necessaria, sive adiaphora, lata à persona vel communitate non habente legislatoriam potestatem, non obligant in Conscientia. Ut si Praetor Urbanus Leges ferret huic Academiae; ut vicinus paterfamilias servum meum juberet boves meos jungere, segetes suas occare, &c. Aut collecta hominum seditiosorum manus in aliqua Angliae Comitatu, (quod in agro Norfolciensi, Eduardo sexto regnante sub Ketto duce, alibique aliquoties factum est) incolis certam pecuniae summam, aut operarum servitutem sibi indebitam publicatis edictis imperaret, eósque vi & armis ad imperata facienda cogerent: utut eis forte liceret (posito quòd resistendo pares non essent) imperata facere; ejusmodi tamen jussu neminem censeri ad ea observanda obligarent in Conscientia. Tum quia ejusmodi Leges, nomine tenus duntaxat, aequivocè Leges sunt, re autem {*} Aquin. 1. 2 qu. 96. art. 4. vera Violentia magis quàm Leges: Et causa aequivoca non infert effectum; sicut non obligat partes lata à Judice sententia. Tum quia vis obligandi ([?]

page.notes: The Greek words in the first line are only partly legible and the text is marked as illegible where I could not read them. The left margin note is marked with an asterisk in the text; the asterisk is placed before "vera". Some numbers near the left edge of the scan (Gen. 28, Psal. 119. 106) are partly cut off and are marked [?]. The last line of the page is cut off by the edge of the scan, and its remaining words are not legible. The "1" in "illicita" and the line-end hyphen in "Patri-archa" are uncertain. The running head is taken from the printed title line.
